title: Seasonal Component Audit — 13 Seasonal Strategies
note: All trade counts are estimates based on typical seasonal entry/exit window frequency. No backtest data exists in the repo for these components. Brain access required to validate.

components.label: SPY / S&P 500 Seasonal
components.seasonalThesis: S&P 500 exhibits well-documented seasonal strength in Q4 (October recovery, year-end rally) and post-correction windows in spring. January effect and 'sell in May' patterns are widely observed.
components.entryWindow: Approximately late September / early October and late December / early January
components.exitWindow: Approximately April / May (spring highs) and March (year-start target)
components.dataRequired: MES OHLC 2008-2026, seasonal signal definition from Brain
components.oosNote: 56 total trades across 18.52yr = 3 trades/yr. Statistical significance extremely low without at least 100+ OOS trades.

components.label: ZM1 / Soybean Meal Seasonal
components.seasonalThesis: Soybean Meal tends to show seasonal strength in summer (July-August) driven by US crop weather uncertainty, and weakness in autumn post-harvest.
components.dataRequired: MZM OHLC 2008-2026 (verify IBKR availability of MZM micro), seasonal signal from Brain
components.oosNote: 37 trades total — insufficient for robust WF. Season pattern may be noise without cross-market validation.

components.label: SB / Sugar Seasonal (Long)
components.seasonalThesis: Sugar #11 (SB) historically shows seasonal strength in spring (March-May) driven by global supply dynamics and Northern Hemisphere demand buildup. Brazilian harvest risk premium in Q1-Q2.
components.dataRequired: SB OHLC 2008-2026. Note: no micro contract for SB — full contract required, increasing margin and risk.
components.oosNote: SB cost (€5/rt) is the highest in the seasonal group. Cost drag per trade is significant — requires edge >€5/rt to be viable.
components.additionalRisk: No SB micro contract. Full contract margin ~€980. Illiquid sessions may cause fill issues.

components.label: HG / Copper Seasonal
components.seasonalThesis: Copper tends to rally in spring (March-May) driven by global construction season pickup and Chinese demand front-running. Summer often sees consolidation.
components.dataRequired: MHG OHLC 2008-2026. Margin ~€1,633 at current levels — high relative to €15-20k portfolio.
components.oosNote: MHG margin is the highest among micro seasonal components. Capital constraint at €15-20k may limit to excluding this component.

components.label: GC1 / Gold Seasonal
components.seasonalThesis: Gold shows seasonal strength in January (post-year-end accumulation, Indian wedding season), late summer (August-September, Indian festival demand, dollar seasonal weakness), and November-December.
components.entryWindow: Approximately late December and late July
components.dataRequired: MGC OHLC 2008-2026. Note: 2nd MGC contract when GLD_BestMonths also active — check simultaneity.
components.simultaneityRisk: GLD_BestMonths (D1 component) and GC1_sea may have overlapping gold positions. Treat as correlated — combined gold exposure must be risk-managed.

components.label: CL / Crude Oil Seasonal
components.seasonalThesis: Crude oil shows seasonal strength in spring (April-May, US driving season ramp-up) and late summer (peak demand). Winter often sees inventory build and price weakness.
components.additionalRisk: Crude oil is the most event-driven commodity — geopolitical events (OPEC decisions, Middle East, Russia) can overwhelm seasonal patterns in any given year. Seasonal edge in crude requires very wide OOS validation.

components.label: ZC / Corn Seasonal
components.seasonalThesis: Corn shows multiple seasonal windows: spring planting uncertainty (April-May rally), summer drought risk premium (June-July), and autumn harvest pressure (September-October weakness). Pre-planting rally is the strongest documented pattern.
components.entryWindow: Approximately March 15 - April 15 (pre-planting), June 15 - July 1 (drought premium)
components.dataRequired: MZC OHLC 2008-2026. Confirm MZC micro availability on IBKR.

components.label: ZW / Wheat Seasonal
components.seasonalThesis: Winter wheat (CBOT ZW) shows seasonal strength in May-June as US winter wheat harvest begins (weather risk premium) and in October-November (new crop planting). Spring rally into harvest is the most reliable documented pattern.
components.dataRequired: MZW OHLC 2008-2026. ZW standard confirmed at €4.92/rt; MZW micro estimated €2.00/rt — confirm with IBKR.
components.oosNote: 37 total trades = 2/yr. Even 6/6 positive WF folds could be random at this trade frequency. Treat as LOW_SAMPLE — not NO_DATA since the thesis is well-established.
components.note: ZW seasonal thesis is one of the best-documented in agricultural seasonality literature.

components.label: ZS / Soybean Seasonal
components.seasonalThesis: Soybeans show seasonal strength in spring (April-May, pre-planting uncertainty), summer (July-August, South American new crop expectations), and post-harvest lows in October. Export demand cycle adds seasonal pattern.

components.label: CC / Cocoa Seasonal
components.seasonalThesis: Cocoa shows seasonal patterns tied to West African crop cycles. Main crop harvest (September-February) tends to produce price weakness; mid-crop (April-July) and weather uncertainty periods tend to produce rallies.
components.additionalRisk: CC (Cocoa) has no micro contract. Full contract required. Margin ~€1,470. Combined with high ICEUS fees (€5/rt), this is the most capital-intensive seasonal component after SB.
components.capitalConstraint: At €20k, CC margin = 7.35% of capital. If included alongside MHG, SB, and full portfolio, marginal margin stack becomes very tight.

components.label: IWM / Russell 2000 Seasonal
components.seasonalThesis: Small-cap stocks (Russell 2000) show January effect (strong January performance), autumn seasonal strength (October-November recovery from Q3 weakness), and tax-loss selling pressure in December that reverses in January.
components.entryWindow: Approximately December 20 - January 5 (January effect entry), October 1 - October 15 (autumn strength)
components.dataRequired: M2K OHLC 2008-2026 (or RTY for pre-M2K period). Seasonal signal definition required from Brain. M2K launched 2019 — earlier history requires RTY approximation with 1/10 scaling.
components.instrumentNote: M2K (multiplier $5) is the confirmed liquid micro equivalent. RTY ($50 multiplier) for larger capital (€25k+). M2K history starts 2019; 2008-2018 period requires RTY price-scaled proxy.
components.oosNote: 37 estimated trades. January effect is well-documented but may be weakening in recent years — requires 2015-2026 OOS test to confirm persistence.

components.label: YM1 TAT (Dow Jones Trend-and-Trade — semi-seasonal)
components.seasonalThesis: Not purely seasonal — TAT (Trend And Trade) is a hybrid trend-following + seasonal system on Dow futures. 573 trades over 18.52yr = 30.9/yr suggests systematic (not purely seasonal) trading.
components.entryWindow: Multiple per year — systematic trend signals
components.dataRequired: MYM OHLC + TAT signal definition from Brain. No PB variant data in repo.
components.note: 573 trades is a reasonable sample. LOW_SAMPLE classification is due to absence of WF validation in current repo, not insufficient raw trade count.

summary.dataRequirement: Full seasonal validation requires Brain OHLC data for MES, MZM, SB, MHG, MGC, MCL, MZC, MZW, MZS, CC, M2K, MYM instruments spanning 2008-2026
